impact.why_not_5: It measures legal instruments against explicit cartels, but the threat that matters, silent coordination, gets no tested countermeasure; one provider, one toy game.
impact.one_change_for_5: A pre-registered price-screen authority arm (K3) that targets silent coordination, with its false-positive rate on Nash players, then an adaptive colluder told the screen rule.
impact.feasibility_why: The screen arm fits budget and time; the evasion arm and threshold choice risk being post hoc under deadline.

execution.why_not_5: Four pools per regime, collapsed reward intervals, 10 and 4 cartels, one provider; Sonnet has 2 pools and no no-channel baseline for its headline silent-coordination claim.
execution.one_change_for_5: Sonnet on 4 pools plus a no-channel arm (K2), Haiku core regimes on 8 pools, with a permutation test over pools beside the bootstrap.
execution.feasibility_why: About 20 USD, runs of 15 to 20 minutes in parallel, and the analysis pipeline already exists.

presentation.why_not_5: Printed title contradicts the text title, Table 3 splits digits across lines, Figure 1 labels overlap, and the running text buries each finding under numbers.
presentation.one_change_for_5: K6: one consistent testbed title, rebuilt Table 3 and Figure 1, numbers moved into tables, each regime paragraph opened by one plain claim.
presentation.feasibility_why: Layout and wording only, about three hours, no API cost.

K1.risk_note: Recidivism rests on few convictions; eight pools may still leave the interval across zero.

K2.risk_note: Sonnet no-channel price may differ from prohibited regimes, complicating the clean silent-coordination story.

K3.risk_note: Screen threshold chosen after seeing data looks tuned; false positives only on scripted Nash players, not adaptive agents.

K4.risk_note: Stated reasons may be unfaithful; a model judging its own family adds little evidential weight.

K5.risk_note: Account may stay locked; local open models may fail the positive control or answer invalid JSON.

K6.risk_note: Trimming numbers from text could drop a caveat the claims depend on.

package.why: K2 gives silent coordination its baseline, K3 turns it into a tested countermeasure with false positives, K1 and K6 are cheap. About 24 hours, 40 USD. K4 is weak evidence, K5 blocked by credits.

five_realistic.why: A screen that catches what leniency misses, with honest false positives, would be shareable. Execution stays capped by one provider and small samples. Presentation needs consistent title and clean tables.

stable_optimum: 4/4/4: K6 lifts presentation reliably, K2 and K1 harden execution, and impact reaches 5 only if the screen arm lands clean and pre-registered.
missing_candidate: An adaptive-adversary arm: tell colluding agents the authority's detection rule (reports or screen) and measure evasion, so the instruments are red-teamed against a strategic opponent, not only observed on compliant agents.
